newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada daily lumber export figures to U.S..

text.p: Canada softwood lumber exports to the United States as of 0001 EST on March 4 in board feet, according to data from the Canadian Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade:
For the Jan 1 - March 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 10.43 million 9.58 million 8.90 million 41.19 million 70.10 mln
EB 1.11 bln 135.57 million 179.32 million 330.11 million 1.76 bln
LFB 56.12 million 5.88 million 24.24 million 37.36 million 123.60 mln
UFB 24.60 million 7.27 million 34.06 million 68.82 million 134.75 mln
Pct exported: EB - 11.96, LFB - 19.01
For the Oct 1 - Dec 31 quarter:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 6.36 million 7.66 million 9.25 million 51.04 million 74.30 mln
EB 2.11 bln 303.43 million 413.03 million 893.02 million 3.72 bln
LFB 3.90 million 10.59 million 6.47 million 11.66 million 32.63 mln
UFB 6.74 million 12.34 million 4.45 million 28.03 million 51.57 mln
Pct exported: EB - 25.28, LFB - 5.01
April 1 - present:
Province BC Alberta Ontario Quebec Total
bonus 16.79 million 17.23 million 18.15 million 90.43 million 142.60 mln
EB 7.86 bln 1.08 bln 1.54 bln 3.33 bln 13.81 bln
LFB 122.62 million 21.22 million 59.31 million 126.56 million 329.70 mln
UFB 31.35 million 19.61 million 38.51 million 96.85 million 186.31 mln
Pct exported: EB - 93.96, LFB - 50.72.
Source: Export and Import Controls Bureau, Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.
NOTE: EB = established base shipments, LFB = lower fee base, UFB = upper base fee.

From April 1, Canadian lumber exports which exceed quarterly or annual quotas are subject to export fee Exports above 14.7 billion board feet annually or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly are subject to US$50 fee for every 1,000 board feet. If such excess exports exceed 650 million board feet, they are subject to a US$100 fee for every 1,000 board feet.
Export quotas are allocated for each province on a company-by-company basis. Shippers who have not been given an allocation are subject to the US$100 fee for any lumber they export.

This export data is based on Canadian export permits. There is a one-week lag between the entry of softwood lumber into the United States and the application for a Canadian permit. ((Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745))
